questions.stem: At dynamic equilibrium, the concentrations of reactants and products remain constant. A student claims this means the reactions have stopped. Is this correct?

options.text: Yes, both reactions stop when equilibrium is reached
No, both forward and reverse reactions are still occurring at equal rates
Yes, the constant concentrations prove no reactions are happening
No, only the forward reaction continues

questions.explanation: Dynamic equilibrium means both the forward and reverse reactions are still occurring, but at equal rates. Products are being formed at the same rate they are being converted back to reactants. This is why it is called 'dynamic' (moving) rather than 'static' (still). Concentrations are constant because the rates of formation and removal balance exactly.

questions.stem: Which conditions are required for a system to reach dynamic equilibrium?

options.text: The reaction must be exothermic and occur at high temperature
The reaction must be reversible and occur in a closed system
The reaction must be fast and occur at high pressure
A catalyst must be present in a sealed container

questions.explanation: Two conditions are needed: (1) the reaction must be reversible (so both forward and reverse reactions can occur), and (2) it must be in a closed system (so no substances can enter or escape). Without a closed system, products may escape and the reverse reaction cannot proceed. A catalyst is not required - it helps reach equilibrium faster but is not necessary.

questions.stem: A sealed container holds a mixture of N2O4 (colourless) and NO2 (brown) at equilibrium. The mixture appears light brown. If a catalyst were added, what would happen to the colour?

options.text: The colour would become darker brown
The colour would become lighter
The colour would remain the same because a catalyst does not change the equilibrium position
The colour would fluctuate between light and dark

questions.explanation: A catalyst speeds up both the forward and reverse reactions equally. It does not change the position of equilibrium or the concentrations of reactants and products at equilibrium. Therefore, the ratio of N2O4 to NO2 remains the same, and the colour stays the same light brown. The catalyst only helps the system reach equilibrium faster.

questions.stem: At equilibrium in a closed container, the rate of the forward reaction equals the rate of the reverse reaction. If the forward rate suddenly increases due to a change in conditions, what happens next?

options.text: The reverse rate stays the same and the system moves away from equilibrium permanently
More products are formed, which increases the reverse rate until a new equilibrium is established
The forward rate immediately returns to its original value
Both rates drop to zero

questions.explanation: When the forward rate increases, more products form. The increasing product concentration then drives the reverse reaction faster. Eventually, the forward and reverse rates become equal again at new equilibrium concentrations. The system adjusts to re-establish equilibrium, but at a new position with different concentrations.

questions.stem: A sealed flask contains the equilibrium: 2SO2(g) + O2(g) ⇌ 2SO3(g). At equilibrium, there are 0.4 mol SO2, 0.2 mol O2, and 0.6 mol SO3. What does 'equilibrium position lies to the right' mean?

options.text: The reaction only goes in the forward direction
There are more moles of products than reactants at equilibrium
The reverse reaction is faster than the forward reaction
All the reactants have been converted to products

questions.explanation: When the equilibrium position lies to the right, it means the concentration of products is greater than the concentration of reactants at equilibrium. Here, 0.6 mol SO3 (product) compared to 0.4 mol SO2 + 0.2 mol O2 (reactants). Both forward and reverse reactions still occur at equal rates - 'lies to the right' just describes the relative amounts.
